To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel adenovirus type-3 (Ad3)-based EV71 vaccine vector that can be used to express a neutralizing B cell antigenic epitope (SP70) from the capsid protein VP-1 of EV71 and that can be used as a promising vaccine candidate for EV71.
a novel EV71 vaccine candidate based on Ad3 vector with a SP70 epitope incorporated in the hexon was developed.
the SP70 neutralizing epitope of enterovirus 71 was successfully incorporated within the hexon of adenovirus type-3 (Ad3), which resulted in the generation of a novel vaccine candidate against EV71.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of adenovirus vectors as vaccine carriers and as epitope delivery vehicles.
the construction of Ad3-based EV 71 vaccine vectors by the incorporation of a neutralizing B cell antigen epitope SP70 into different surface-exposed regions of the capsid hexon.
the construction of Ad-based EV71 vaccine vector by incorporation of neutralizing epitope into hexon of Ad.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ad3-based EV 71 vaccine vector containing SP70 within the HVR1 or 2 of hexon is promising for the protection against EV71.
Ad3-based hexon-modified EV71 vaccines are promising for the prevention of EV71 infections in children.
this study provides valuable evidence for hexon-modification of Ad3 as a promising EV 71 vaccine candidate and also as an epitope delivery vehicle for other pathogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SP70 neutralizing epitope was incorporated into the hypervariable regions (HVR) of the hexons of Ad3EGF, and the resulting recombinant Ads conferred protection in vivo against the lethal EV 71 challenge in neonatal mice, and that the SP70-modified Ads were safe and effective as an epitope delivery platform.
we successfully incorporated neutralizing B-cell epitope SP70 into Ad3 capsid, the modified Ad3 could elicit SP70-specific humoral immune response and confer protection against EV71 challenge.
the Ad-based EV71 vaccine candidates with neutralizing epitopes incorporated in the surface-exposed domain of the hexon could be promising candidates for further evaluation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Ad3 vector-based vaccine can be developed to confer protection against EV71, and the SP70 epitopes can be incorporated into the HVR1 and HVR2 regions of the Ad3 hexon without affecting the virus fitness.
the hexon-modified adenovirus type-3 vector can be a promising EV71 subunit vaccine candidate and an epitope-delivery vehicle for other pathogens.
the Ad3 vector is a promising EV71 candidate vaccine, and it can also serve as a platform to deliver epitopes of other pathogens.
